headline: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said the United States "absolutely must" work with Chinese AI companies and keep talking with China so AI develops safely.
score_reason: A top chip-industry leader publicly backs US-China AI cooperation, but it is one executive's view, not a policy or agreement.
importance_line: People everywhere gain if the two AI powers coordinate on safety, but the call comes from Jensen Huang, whose company sells chips to the industry and who opposes overly strict rules.
summary: CNBC reports, as relayed by BigGo Finance, that Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia, the world's leading AI chip maker, told it in London on 14 Oct 2026 that the US "absolutely must" work with Chinese AI companies, describing AI as "powerful and potentially dangerous". He urged more dialogue, said the UK should do the same, and repeated his opposition to overly strict rules; his remarks followed Nvidia's pledge of $250 million over five years to UK AI safety research.
notes: CNBC and the CNA clip were blocked or empty; text read via BigGo Finance, which summarises the CNBC report. Huang spoke Wed 14 Oct in London; reporting is 15 Oct. Url is the CNBC link named by the search result.
